title: EA-CORPORA-34 — The Thirty-Fourth Seating: Secondary Source — the Reception of the Apocalypse, from the Fathers to the Critics (Eusebius, Irenaeus, Justin, the Muratorian Fragment, Epiphanius, the Catalogues, Toledo IV, Luther 1522, Erasmus, the Critics 1886–1920, Gregory; and the Carriage: Scrivener, Delitzsch, Tregelles, Erasmus 1516)
creator: Cranes, Rebekah
description: The thirty-fourth seating of the originals shelf, eleven seats, the sources of Secondary Source, the reception study of how the Apocalypse came to be received as derivative, secondary and marginal, seated before drafting: Eusebius's Historia ecclesiastica in Greek (Dindorf); Irenaeus in Harvey's Greek and Latin; Justin's Dialogue; the Muratorian fragment in Tregelles's edition; Epiphanius's Panarion (Holl); Westcott's survey with the catalogues of the first eight centuries; the Collectio Hispana with the Fourth Council of Toledo; Luther's September Testament of 1522; Erasmus's Annotationes; Vischer, Spitta, Gunkel, Bousset and Charles; and Gregory's Textkritik for the manuscripts and lectionaries; and, at v1.1, the carriage of the book: Scrivener's Plain Introduction (1894), Delitzsch's Handschriftliche Funde (1861) on Reuchlin's codex, Tregelles's Account of the Printed Text (1854) on the last six verses supplied from the Latin, and Erasmus's Novum Instrumentum of 1516.
substrate: Human–machine collaborative. Rebekah Cranes is a heteronym of Lee Sharks, the standing authority on the EA-CORPORA deposits (named by the author on 2026-11-04 and held at his word of 2026-11-05). methodology: Each seat fetched in session from the source its record names (First1KGreek, the Internet Archive), kept as served, reduced to a text layer by code and hashed into its MANIFEST.sha256; licences read at the file; loci verified by substring in the text layer, the Greek loci in the TEI's own code points; public-domain status checked against first publication and the editor's death. No text corrected by hand. The builders and this body are under rebuild/corpora/ea-corpora-34/.
falsification_conditions: A seat is falsified if its files do not verify against its MANIFEST.sha256 at the canonical URL; if a verified locus is absent from the text layer it names; if a work is misattributed, misdated or assigned to the wrong edition; if a licence recorded for an item is not the one its source states; if a work seated as public domain is not, in the jurisdiction stated; or if the four surfaces (seat, index, deposit, shelf) disagree.

wiki_article: EA-CORPORA-34 is the thirty-fourth seating of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive's originals shelf, deposited under Rebekah Cranes, the standing authority on the EA-CORPORA deposits, on 5 November 2026. Its fifteen seats, 24 works and some 819,000 lines of text layer carry the sources of Secondary Source, the reception study of how the Apocalypse came to be received as derivative, secondary and marginal, seated before the study is drafted. The fathers come first: Eusebius's Historia ecclesiastica in Dindorf's Greek (34/01), with the ledger of the books, Gaius, Papias's two Johns, Irenaeus's sentence on Domitian and Dionysius on Nepos; Irenaeus in Harvey's Greek and Latin (34/02); Justin's Dialogue with Trypho (34/03), where John, one of the apostles, prophesies in a revelation made to him; the Muratorian fragment in Tregelles's edition of 1867 (34/04), whose Paul writes to seven churches following the order of his predecessor John; and Epiphanius's Panarion (34/05), with the Alogi. The fourth-century catalogues are read in Westcott's appendix of the original texts (34/06); the Fourth Council of Toledo, whose seventeenth canon ascribes the Apocalypse to John and requires it to be read, in the Collectio Hispana (34/07). Luther's September Testament of 1522 (34/08) and Erasmus's Annotationes (34/09) hold the Reformation's printed judgments; Vischer, Spitta, Gunkel, Bousset and Charles (34/10) the criticism of 1886 to 1920; and Gregory's Textkritik (34/11) the manuscripts and lectionaries. Twenty loci are verified in the seated texts, the Greek given in the code points of the First1KGreek TEI. Version 1.1 (5 November 2026) adds the carriage of the book (34/12–34/15): Scrivener's Plain Introduction (1894), Delitzsch's Handschriftliche Funde (1861), Tregelles's Account of the Printed Text (1854) and Erasmus's Novum Instrumentum of 1516, for the one manuscript from which the first printed Apocalypse was made and the last six verses supplied from the Latin.
